text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.04% today as oil prices surged on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. A container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz amid Iranian attacks on commercial shipping, and Saudi Aramco facilities came under fresh assault—both events that threaten to disrupt global oil supplies and push crude prices higher. With Brent crude at $125 a barrel (a significant premium to the US price of $96), the market is pricing in real supply risk, which directly benefits an oil producer's margins and revenues.

The stock's broader two-week surge of nearly 14% reflects months of mounting Middle East tensions finally translating into sustained higher oil prices. Analysts are now warning of diesel supply shortages stretching into 2027, which signals this supply crunch may not be temporary—a structural tailwind for producers who benefit from extended periods of elevated energy costs.
